header: THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, CIRCUIT COURT, HYDERABAD
[Muhammad Waseem Khan v. Late Inayatullah Memon (deceased) through LRs]
Respondent : Late Inayatullah Memon (deceased) through LRs
body: Muhammad Humayun Khan, J.- Through this Civil Revision Application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (the Code), the applicant has called in question the order dated 25.07.2026 (the impugned order), passed by the learned VIII Additional District Judge, Hyderabad (the trial Court), in Summary Suit No.46 of 2022, whereby his application under section 12(2) of the Code, seeking to set aside the judgment and decree dated 27.08.2025, was dismissed as not maintainable.

2. Briefly stated, the predecessor-in-interest of the respondents instituted a suit under Order XXXVII of the Code for recovery of Rs.800,000/- on the basis of two dishonoured cheques of Rs.400,000/- each. The applicant was granted leave to defend on 26.05.2022. He filed his written statement denying the tenancy as well as the issuance of the cheques, whereafter issues were framed. The attorney of the plaintiff was examined and produced documents in evidence. Despite sufficient opportunities, the applicant neither cross-examined the witness nor led evidence in defence. Consequently, his side was closed on 17.04.2025. The suit was decreed on merits on 27.08.2025. Instead of preferring an appeal, the applicant, on 23.04.2026, filed an application under section 12(2) of the Code, which was dismissed through the impugned order. Civil Revision Application No.S-177 of 2026 Page 2 of 3 3. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and perused the record available with the memo of revision.

4. The revisional jurisdiction of this Court under section 115 of the Code is limited to cases where the subordinate Court has exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law, has failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested, or has acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity. Such jurisdiction cannot be exercised as a substitute for appellate jurisdiction, nor can this Court merely substitute its discretion for that of the subordinate Court. In this regard, reliance is placed on Sardar Muhammad Kamal-ud-Din Khan v. Syed Munir Syed (2022 SCMR 806).

5. Section 12(2) of the Code provides a remedy against a judgment, decree or order on the ground of fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction. It cannot be invoked merely to reopen matters which could have been agitated in an appeal. In the instant case, the applicant appeared through counsel, obtained leave to defend, filed his written statement and participated in the proceedings. Despite sufficient opportunities, he failed to cross-examine the plaintiff’s witness or lead evidence. Such failure, by itself, does not constitute fraud or misrepresentation. In the absence of specific grounds attracting section 12(2) of the Code, the remedy against the decree lay in a regular appeal. Reliance in this regard is placed on Mst.Musarat Parveen v. Muhammad Yousaf (2023 SCMR 1665).

6. The allegations regarding fabrication of the rent agreement and issuance of the cheques in connection with an oral transaction for the sale of tiles pertain to the merits of the original claim. The latter plea is also inconsistent with the written statement, wherein the applicant denied having issued the cheques. No particulars have been furnished to show how the decree was procured through fraud or misrepresentation, nor has any want of Civil Revision Application No.S-177 of 2026 Page 3 of 3 jurisdiction been demonstrated. The discrepancy in the execution number mentioned in the newspaper publication relates to proceedings subsequent to the decree and does not, by itself, affect its validity. The plea regarding denial of opportunity is also belied by the order dated 17.04.2025, which shows that the applicant’s side was closed after sufficient opportunities had been afforded to him. In these circumstances, the trial Court was justified in dismissing the application without framing issues or recording evidence thereon.

7. In view of the above, learned counsel for the applicant has failed to point out any jurisdictional defect, illegality or material irregularity in the impugned order within the contemplation of section 115 of the Code, or any misreading or non-reading of the record warranting interference by this Court. Consequently, this Civil Revision Application is dismissed in limine. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
